raw:
Queries target the known interaction effects in NAS-Bench-201: whether a path from input to output exists, how skip and conv ops combine, and the patterns seen in the best cells.

1. Edge-level interactions here mostly come from connectivity. Setting an edge to 'none' can cut every path to the output or isolate node 1 or 2. Swapping a parameter-free op for a conv matters most when that edge lies on the only conv-bearing path.
2. Top cells usually have nor_conv_3x3 on most edges and a skip on edge 3 (node 0 -> node 3). Too many skip or pooling edges causes collapse, as in DARTS.
3. Rankings are highly correlated across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16-120. Studies of operation importance and epistasis (e.g., fANOVA-style analyses) speak directly to whether an interaction holds consistently across the three datasets.
